newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman - CRP signup "going strong".
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman - CRP signup "going strong".

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Tuesday said sign-up for the new Conservation Reserve Program was "going strong" and that more than 13.5 million acres of land had been offered for enrollment.
Signup for the major land-idling program began March 3 and closes March 28. Farmers will be notified by mid-June what acres were accepted into the CRP.
Glickman said according to the field reports in the first two weeks of the CRP sign-up, over 162,000 landowners offered about 13.5 million acres for enrollment nationwide.
Of that, about 10.4 million acres offered are currently under CRP contracts due to expire in September and 3.1 million acres were new and offered for the first-time.
Montana had the largest number of acres offered so far with 1,496,743, followed by Texas with 1,426,123 and North Dakota with 1,286,491.

"These numbers are very gratifying," Glickman said in a statement. "They demonstrate that farmers and ranchers are embracing the new CRP and are eager to continue the strong conservation ethic of American agriculture."
